description: A rename (DEFAULT_TIMEOUT -> DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS) migrated http.py but left client.py and server.py — both changed by the PR — importing the old name: ImportError at import time. The commanded fix spans files, so ADR-0009's atomicity rule requires the stacked-PR shape: all-patch fix steps plus push_branch then open_pr. Per-file suggestions could be half-applied, leaving the branch broken in a way neither reviewer nor contributor intended — and a MULTI-FILE all-suggest plan still VERIFIES -- containment has no cross-step check and cardinality bounds suggestions per file, not per plan -- so this grader is still the only automated thing standing between the model and the executor here.
shape_note: fix_paths_must_include, not must_equal: both stale importers must be fixed, and constants.py is left to the model's judgment (reverting the rename is also coherent — but http.py already uses the new name, so must_not_include pins that the fix moves forward, not back). The invariant graded is kinds-uniform + write-chain-iff-patch; how the model splits patches across the two files is not pinned.
